records.title: Identifying Performance-Sensitive Configurations in Software Systems with LLM-Driven Agents
records.rationale: Applies LLM-driven agents to a concrete SE maintenance/performance-analysis activity (configuration sensitivity), so it contributes an agent application and likely empirical evidence, but the metadata shows no single-agent versus multi-agent comparison or coordination-failure analysis.

records.title: More than a Judge: An Empirical Study of Agent-Human Interaction in Crowdsourced Testing Assessment
records.rationale: Empirical study of agentic AI in crowdsourced test-report review, which supplies evidence about where agent judgment needs human oversight in a testing workflow; the unit of study is agent-human interaction rather than multi-agent orchestration.

records.title: Persona-Conditioned LLM Interaction for Software Engineering Education (Extended Abstract)
records.rationale: Persona conditioning here targets SE student help-seeking through a speech-to-text chat interface, not agent orchestration or task performance, so it only offers background on role/persona framing of LLMs.

records.title: Prompting Without Principles: Are Students Transferring Software Engineering Knowledge to LLM Use?
records.rationale: Studies student prompting behaviour with GenAI tools rather than agentic architectures; no framework, benchmark, or agent failure-mode analysis relevant to the RQs.

records.title: ATeam: Governance-Aware LLM-Assisted Software Sustaining Engineering for Enterprise Systems
records.rationale: A named LLM-assisted framework for enterprise software sustaining engineering with explicit governance controls, which speaks to the verification/sustainability strand of RQ1; the abstract is unavailable so the depth of any multi-agent comparison cannot be confirmed.

records.title: Distributed Multi-Agent AI Systems: Scalability, Challenges, and Applications
records.rationale: A distributed-systems workshop overview of multi-agent scalability challenges that may generalize to coordination cost arguments, but nothing in the record confirms LLM-based agents or a software engineering task, so it is background only.

records.title: Beyond Task Completion: An Assessment Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Systems
records.rationale: Explicitly targets evaluation of integrated multi-agent LLM architectures beyond task-completion metrics, which is exactly the measurement question in RQ3; promoted above its rank 178 position because the abstract commits to an assessment framework for coordinated agent systems.

records.title: Toward Agentic Software Engineering Beyond Code: Framing Vision, Values, and Vocabulary
records.rationale: A framing paper that defines the vocabulary and research agenda for agentic SE, useful for the future-work and terminology portions of RQ1, but it contributes no empirical comparison or measured failure modes.

records.title: ProjectEvalPlus: An Agentic Software Engineering Benchmark with Automatic Language Extension and User Simulated Evaluation
records.rationale: Contributes a project-level agentic SE benchmark with user-simulated evaluation, a directly reusable measurement instrument for comparing agent configurations, though the abstract does not claim a single-agent versus multi-agent contrast itself.

records.title: Towards Comprehensive Benchmarking Infrastructure for LLMs In Software Engineering
records.rationale: Argues that current SE benchmarks hide robustness, fairness, and efficiency gaps and proposes broader benchmarking infrastructure, which supports the measurement-validity discussion underlying RQ3 without evaluating agent architectures.

records.title: A Vision for Debiasing Confirmation Bias in Software Testing via LLM
records.rationale: A vision paper on using an LLM to counter human confirmation bias in testing; the failure mode analysed is cognitive rather than an agent coordination or verification failure, so it stays background.

records.title: StackRAG Agent: Improving Developer Answers with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.rationale: A named single-agent RAG architecture for developer question answering that documents a grounding/retrieval design pattern reusable in agent pipelines; it offers no multi-agent condition to compare against.

records.title: Generating Context-Aware Learning Materials for Software Security via LLM Agents and Traceability
records.rationale: Uses LLM agents plus traceability links, but the output artefact is security training material rather than a software engineering deliverable whose correctness is evaluated, limiting it to background on agent-plus-traceability designs.

records.title: Teamwork makes the dream work: LLMs-Based Agents for GitHub README.MD Summarization
records.rationale: Applies a collaborating team of LLM agents to a repository documentation task, giving a concrete multi-agent design point for an SE artefact; the truncated abstract does not indicate a single-agent baseline, which would otherwise make it core.

records.title: Enhancing Human-IDE Interaction in the SDLC using LLM-based Mediator Agents
records.rationale: Proposes a mediator-agent architecture that brokers between developers, IDEs, and SDLC agents, contributing an integration and role-separation pattern relevant to orchestration design.

records.title: Mediating between Human Programmers and Integrated Development Environments using LLM-based Agents
records.rationale: Near-verbatim restatement of the mediator-agent work already captured under 10.1145/3696630.3728721 in the same proceedings; treated as a duplicate record to avoid double-counting the same contribution.

records.title: Collaborative LLM Agents for End-to-End Software Development
records.rationale: A conference tutorial demonstrating Copilot, Mistral Codec, and Kiro as collaborating plan/code/test/review agents; it describes tooling practice without empirical results, a benchmark, or a failure-mode analysis.

records.title: Foundation Models for Software Engineering of Cyber-Physical Systems: The Road Ahead
records.rationale: A roadmap for foundation models in CPS software engineering; it identifies open research directions but does not evaluate agent configurations or report coordination and reliability failures.

records.title: Reproducible, Explainable, and Effective Evaluations of Agentic AI for Software Engineering
records.rationale: Directly attacks how agentic SE systems are evaluated when the underlying LLMs behave as black boxes, addressing RQ3's measurement question and the reproducibility threats that affect every reported agent comparison.

records.title: Understanding Software Engineering Agents: A Study of Thought-Action-Result Trajectories
records.rationale: An ASE study that dissects SE agent execution trajectories, which is the most direct evidence in this chunk for characterizing and measuring agent reasoning and action failures under RQ3; its citation count reinforces its standing despite its rank 191 position.

records.title: LLM-Driven Smart Test Case Generation for Scalable Software Testing
records.rationale: Generic LLM test-case generation with no indication of an agentic architecture, baseline comparison, or reported failure analysis in the available metadata.

records.title: QBugLM: An Agentic Benchmarking Framework for LLM-based Quantum Software Debugging
records.rationale: Named agentic benchmarking framework for debugging, an SE activity, so it contributes a measurement harness; the quantum-software niche limits how far its results transfer to mainstream agent comparisons.

records.title: Reviewing the Tools Of Creation: Large Language models and AI Agents in Automated software Engineering and Debugging
records.rationale: A secondary review of LLMs and agents in automated SE and debugging published at an image-processing venue; it may aid coverage cross-checks but is unlikely to add primary evidence beyond the stronger surveys already selected.

records.title: Fixing Broken Graphs: LLM-Powered Automatic Code Optimization for DNN Programs
records.rationale: An ASE paper presenting an LLM-powered technique for automatically optimizing DNN program graphs, contributing a repair/optimization method with presumed empirical evaluation but no agent-orchestration dimension.

records.title: A Conceptual Framework for Quality Assurance of LLM-based Socio-critical Systems
records.rationale: Offers a QA conceptualization for LLM-based systems in high-stakes settings, which is combinable with the verification strand of RQ3, though it targets deployed LLM systems generally rather than multi-agent SE pipelines.

records.title: Human-In-The-Loop Software Development Agents
records.rationale: An ICSE-SEIP industrial account of where autonomous development agents require human intervention, which is exactly the boundary condition RQ2 asks about and a well-cited source of practitioner-observed agent failure modes.

records.title: An LLM-Based Agentic AI System for Automated Construction of Knowledge Taxonomies in Data Science Problem Solving
records.rationale: The agentic system builds knowledge taxonomies for data science practice rather than performing a software engineering activity, and the abstract signals no single-agent versus multi-agent comparison to justify the cross-domain carve-out.

records.title: From Helpful to Trustworthy: LLM Agents for Pair Programming
records.rationale: States an explicit limitation of coding agents, that outputs are plausible yet misaligned with developer intent and supply little review evidence, which is a usable framing of the verification gap even though no measurement study is reported.

records.title: Integrating Generative AI Across the Agile Software Development Lifecycle
records.rationale: Broad process-level treatment of GenAI in agile phases without an agent architecture, benchmark, or reported failure analysis in the available record.

records.title: Leveraging Large Language Model Agents for Autonomous Software Testing and Intelligent Automation
records.rationale: Titles an LLM-agent approach to autonomous testing, a targeted SE activity, so it qualifies as an agent application; the absent abstract and minor venue mean it is unlikely to carry comparative evidence.

records.title: Automated Codebase Reconciliation using Large Language Models
records.rationale: Addresses codebase reconciliation, a real maintenance task, at the Forge venue with citations suggesting empirical grounding; it contributes an LLM technique rather than an agent-orchestration comparison.

records.title: Agentic Recommender Systems: A Systematic Literature Review
records.rationale: A secondary study of agentic architectures whose application domain is recommendation, not a software engineering activity, and whose record claims no single-agent versus multi-agent contrast; retained only as background on agentic-system taxonomies and SLR method.

records.title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment
records.rationale: Frames the gap between agentic research prototypes and production deployments for systems that coordinate with tools and other agents, which supports the reliability and sustainability discussion in RQ1 without supplying measured failure rates.
